title: miután + Past Tense: What Happened After

sections.title: One past event, then another
sections.content: *miután* ("after") links two events that both already happened, in the order they happened: *miután*-clause first, main clause second — put the past tense in BOTH clauses, exactly the forms you already know. Hungarian has no separate "had happened" tense; *miután* itself does the job of showing which event came first, so both verbs stay in plain past tense. Put a comma between the two clauses.

sections.title: miután + past, past
rows: After we arrived, we went for a walk.
After he finished work, he went home.
After Anna called me, I set off right away.

items.english: After we arrived, we went for a walk.
We went for a walk after we arrived.

sections.content: Watch definiteness as closely as you would in any other past-tense sentence: *Miután elolvastam a levelet, megmutattam Annának* — *elolvastam* is DEFINITE because *a levelet* is a specific, definite object ("the letter"). *miután* doesn't change any of the rules you already know about definite versus indefinite conjugation, it just adds the "after" meaning on top.
